reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents an educational walkthrough of an ANOME task-event post, including its visible participation steps and an educational disclaimer. Although it repeats an earning range and demonstrates check-ins, social-media activity, and proof uploads, the available video evidence describes these as reported or demonstrated claims without establishing deception, theft, impersonation, or a completed transaction.

citations.quote: You easily can do from 1 dollar to 310 dollars
see the links in the description and the link of all the channels, follow the channel and start your campaigns and install offers
download our preview or our screenshot and hit upload
Follow level up official x You have to follow them
if you also do the same task here, then you will get $ 3.

opening.argument: The central message is a low-barrier reward proposition tied to a sequence of viewer actions, not merely general information. The video says viewers can earn as much as $310, directs them to links in the description, and tells them to follow channels, start campaigns, and install offers. It then connects completion to concrete rewards: a daily check-in can lead to an iPhone drawing, and completing the tasks is said to produce dollar payments. The demonstrated flow reinforces that relationship by showing a starter USDT task and additional locked tasks requiring check-ins, social interaction, and proof submission. That is a solicitation to perform actions in exchange for promised value, which is the relevant scam pattern even if the recording does not prove whether every participant ultimately gets paid.

citations.quote: You easily can do from 1 dollar to 310 dollars
follow the channel and start your campaigns and install offers
In order to check in you can join drawing and you can win up to an iPhone
if you also do the same task here, then you will get $ 3.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense understates what the walkthrough asks viewers to do. This is not only a description of a post: it instructs viewers to follow accounts, upload proof, watch content, comment, and like in order to complete the campaign. The video also describes authorizing with Twitter and submitting a wallet address before a daily check-in. Those requested actions, combined with stated rewards, are enough to identify the solicitation; proof of completed theft is not required to recognize the offer as scam-like.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These quotes show a task campaign and participation requirements, but they do not show that the campaign is fraudulent. The video may be encouraging viewers to complete ordinary promotional tasks for stated rewards; authorization and wallet-related steps alone do not establish theft, unauthorized access, or a fake service. The available evidence does not confirm that anyone was charged, lost funds, or was denied a legitimate reward.

citations.quote: today we will join a new company, whose token is already listed, Binance alpha
We have completed 4 task
if you also do the same task here, then you will get $ 3.

opening.argument: The offer combines several warning signals that make the promised benefit materially misleading in presentation: unusually large earnings, crypto-linked rewards, external destinations, account authorization, wallet handling, and escalating task requirements. The video advertises a range up to $310 while also mentioning an iPhone, an NFT valued at $3, and additional dollar payments. Participation is routed through description links and messaging channels, and the process includes Twitter authorization and wallet-address submission. The task page visibly presents a 1 USDT starter reward alongside further locked activities. Taken together, the viewer is drawn by easy money but must surrender attention, social engagement, account access, or wallet information across an external campaign flow. Calling this educational does not neutralize the misleading combination of incentives and data-sensitive steps.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The disclaimer is not evidence that the offer is safe. Nor does describing the rewards as reported eliminate the risk created by promoting a large earning range, external links, account authorization, and wallet submission in one flow. The visible task page adds a starter reward and locked follow-on tasks, while the narration says higher task completion yields more money. That is precisely the kind of low-effort reward funnel a careful review should treat skeptically.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The combination may justify caution, but caution is not proof of a scam. The earning range, NFT statement, and task rewards are claims made in the video; none establishes that the rewards are impossible, that the external pages are malicious, or that wallet information was misused. The educational disclaimer and task walkthrough are consistent with promotion of an ordinary campaign, and the record does not document a victim, a payment demand, or a failed withdrawal.

citations.quote: This video is made for educational purposes only
whose token is already listed, Binance alpha
and how to withdraw these tasks.

opening.argument: The video's educational framing functions as direct promotion because it repeatedly moves the viewer from explanation to participation. It identifies a new token campaign, points viewers to the description and WhatsApp channel, walks through the external site, demonstrates authorization and check-in, and tells viewers how to complete and verify tasks. The call to follow channels, install offers, upload proof, watch a required video, comment, and like is operational guidance designed to increase campaign participation. The claimed rewards supply the inducement: earnings up to $310 and a possible iPhone are presented alongside the steps. A copyright or educational disclaimer does not change the practical effect of this coordinated invitation to join an external reward funnel.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense calls this an educational walkthrough, but its own evidence shows the speaker telling viewers to follow accounts, install offers, upload screenshots, and complete checks. The narration even directs viewers to invite others and promises payment for repeating the tasks. Those are promotional calls to action, not neutral reporting. The disclaimer describes intended purpose; it does not erase the video's practical direction toward an external campaign.

download our preview or our screenshot and hit upload
if you also do the same task here, then you will get $ 3.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Instructional detail does not by itself make the campaign fraudulent. A promotion can explain how to participate, and the available material shows task completion steps rather than a fabricated transaction or proven deception. The description explicitly presents the video as educational, while the cited calls to action establish only that participation is encouraged. They do not show that the campaign or its rewards are false.
